summary: Port reproduces both of the original's visual states (scrolling rainbow + posterized band flash) and matches its 1 Hz / 50%-duty flash cadence for about the first 10 s, but its flash gating then drifts onto a ~150 s super-cycle that leaves it stuck permanently posterized or permanently non-reactive for ~93% of the timeline, and its flash dims rather than brightens.
observations: Rig is a 16x16 grid, 256 px; neither side exposes any control (probe: 'no settable controls' on both). Both sides report wantsSensors:true and were fed the identical beat120 synth signal.

Both sides share the same idle look: a smooth full-spectrum rainbow banded down the linear pixel index, all 256 pixels distinct, peak channel 178, scrolling steadily. Original's idle saturation is slightly lower (min channel 44 of 178, s~0.75) than the port's (min channel 26, s~0.85) — a small but consistent colour difference.

Both sides' 'flash' state is a posterized version of that rainbow: ~4-12 solid colour bands laid along the linear pixel index with black separators. Confirmed by --dump: an original flash frame has exactly 10 distinct colours and 9 black separator runs of exactly 1 px; a port flash frame has 10 colours but 9 separator runs of 2 px plus one long black tail run (13-46 px, i.e. 5-18% of the strip) that the original never draws. Port black pixel counts run 17-46 per frame vs the original's 6-9 (occasionally up to 32).

ORIGINAL flash is a BRIGHTNESS POP: peak channel goes 178 (idle) -> 255 (full value), and mean brightness rises from the idle 111 to 116-148. PORT flash is a DIM: peak channel only reaches 203, and with the extra black its mean brightness FALLS from the idle 102 to 73-96. The direction of the brightness envelope is inverted.

Cadence, first ~10 s at 20 fps: both alternate 0.5 s flash / 0.5 s rainbow on a 1.0 s period (10 frames on, 10 frames off, event starts every 20 frames) against the 2 Hz beat — i.e. both fire on every other beat. They are ANTIPHASE, though: original flashes over t in [k+0.60, k+1.05] s, port over [k+0.05, k+0.50] s (baseline runs: orig event starts at frames 32,52,72,92,112; port at 21,41,61,81,101).

STEADY STATE DIVERGES BADLY. Idle (non-flash) frame fraction per 10 s over a 300 s / 20 fps run — original: 49,50,52,52,50,51,52,51,50,51,52,53,51,51,52,51,50,51,52,52,51,51,53,51,50,51,52,51,50,51 (rock-steady 50/50 for the whole 5 minutes). Port: 53,1,1,1,2,1,1,3,45,90,100,100,100,100,100,100,65,17,1,4,3,2,3,1,31,75,100,100,100,100. The port is correct only for the first ~10 s, then pins to 'always posterized' (t=10-75 s), then to 'never posterized' (t=95-155 s), and repeats on a ~150 s super-cycle.

Confirmed by dump, not just by stats: at t=40.05-41.95 s (0.1 s spacing) the original alternates 255-peak posterize frames with 256-colour rainbow frames every 0.5 s while the port is posterized (11 colours, peak 203) at every single sampled time. At t=100.15-102.35 s the original still alternates while the port is a pure 256-colour rainbow at every sampled time — the music reactivity has vanished entirely.

FRAME-RATE COUPLING of the port's flash trigger. Original flashes at every rate tested (event duty ~50% at 15, 20, 30 and 40 fps, period always 1.0 s). Port produces NO flash at all at 10 fps (60 s survey: mean brightness constant 102 on all 600 frames; a 20 s dump at 10 fps shows a 256-colour rainbow at every sampled time) and only 2 flash frames in 100 at 5 fps, while the original is flashing near-continuously at those rates. At 15/20/30/40 fps the port's early-window cadence does match the original's 1.0 s period / 0.5 s duration.

Resolution behaviour differs on the flash. Re-rendered at --grid 48x48 (2304 px), the original's flash keeps exactly the same structure at the same FRACTIONS of the strip: 9 boundaries at 0.106/0.350/0.494/0.603/0.701/0.797/0.882/0.957/0.998 vs 0.109/0.352/0.496/0.605/0.703/0.797/0.883/0.957/0.992 at 256 px, and separators stay exactly 1 px. The port's flash at 2304 px has ~31 colours and 35 black runs (vs 10 colours / 9 runs at 256 px), and its black tail becomes a ~5 px-pitch comb over the last 5% of the strip instead of a solid run — so the port's band count and tail texture change with pixel count where the original's do not.

With --sensors off both sides degrade identically and gracefully to a static-mean scrolling rainbow with no flashes at all (orig mean 111 flat, port 102 flat, motion 3 each) — so every divergence above is in the audio-reaction path, not in a separate free-running term.

Seed-independent: seed 1234 reproduces the seed-1 event structure frame-for-frame on both sides (orig starts 4,14,32,52,72,76,92,112,...; port 3,7,21,41,61,81,101,...), as expected for a purely sensor-driven pattern.
feedback: Headline fix: the port's flash gating drifts. The original holds a constant 50% duty cycle — 0.5 s posterized flash, 0.5 s rainbow, repeating every 1.0 s — unchanged from t=0 to t=300 s. The port holds that for ~10 s and then latches: stuck posterized from t~10 s to t~75 s, stuck on the plain rainbow from t~95 s to t~155 s, and it cycles between those two failure states about every 150 s. Something in the port's beat/threshold state accumulates instead of tracking; the fix must keep the flash/no-flash decision stationary over minutes, not just over the opening seconds.

The flash must be a brightness POP, not a dim. The original drives the posterized colours to full value (peak channel 255) against an idle rainbow whose peak is 178, so mean brightness rises ~111 -> 116-148 on every flash. The port only reaches 203 (peak +14% instead of +43%), and its mean brightness DROPS to 73-96. Raise the flash value to full and the envelope direction inverts back to the original's.

Halve the black separator width and drop the black tail. The original's posterized frames are separated by exactly ONE black pixel per band boundary, at any rig size, with no dark region anywhere else (6-9 black pixels of 256). The port uses 2-px separators and additionally blacks out a 13-46 px run at the end of the strip, giving 17-46 black pixels of 256. Visually this reads as a shredded, dashed flash where the original reads as clean solid bars.

Make the flash structure resolution-independent. The original draws the SAME number of bands at the SAME fractional positions on a 256 px grid and a 2304 px grid; the port draws ~10 bands at 256 px and ~31 at 2304 px, and its trailing dark region turns from a solid run into a comb. Band boundaries should be computed as fractions of the pixel count, not as fixed pixel counts.

Fix the frame-rate coupling in the trigger. At 10 fps and 5 fps the port never flashes at all over 20-60 s windows while the original flashes throughout; at 15-40 fps the port does fire on the right 1.0 s period. Whatever threshold/decay drives the flash decision is being stepped per frame rather than per unit time, so it never crosses at low frame rates.

Minor, once the above are fixed: the port's flash lands on the opposite half-second of the 1 Hz cycle from the original's (original flashes t in [k+0.60, k+1.05] s, port [k+0.05, k+0.50] s against the same 2 Hz beat), and the idle rainbow is slightly more saturated than the original's (min channel 26 vs 44 against a peak of 178).
Band-count dynamics are also flatter: the original's flash varies between 4 and 11 bands over time as the sequencer advances; the port sits at 8-12 with far less variation.
